items.title: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
Waking up to good news hasn't happened much, lately, so this morning's election results were a wonderful surprise. But, let's not gloat so much. Use that energy to fix things.

I know, it's been quiet here lately. I'm having fun over on the wiki instead.

items.title: Rudimentary Lathe comes out of retirement for the 3rd time
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I miss when a bunch of us weirdos overshared on our TiddlyWikis nearly every day. Most are gone or unmaintained now. Can we bring them back? I'll start: rudimentarylathe.org

Nearly 5,000 notes going back to 2018, and man oh man, at least 4,800 of them are an embarrassment. I should keep this stuff to myself, but that horse left the barn long ago.

We used to write "TiddlyMails" to each other (I don't think we actually called them that). I'd write a note that simply mentioned someone with their own wiki. They'd read it, and write a note on their wiki with a link back and a title something like: "Re: That thing you wrote". It was completely manual and done without pings or notifications of any kind. So fun!

If you have a similar wiki, let me know. I'd love to visit!

TiddlyWiki is more than 20 years old and still a miracle to me.

items.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
When it comes to note-taking software, I prioritize usefulness over longevity. I prefer plain text (e.g. .org and .md files), I prefer having both, but I'm not going to reject an app that makes my notes useful today, due to some kind of functional "lock-in".

I think I need to teach Claude about TiddlyWiki...and Tinderbox.

items.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I hate to admit this, but I kind of miss Lightroom Classic. It was nice having a very good RAW processor and capable catalog with a large ecosystem and all of my photos in one big library. I've spent so much time trying to concoct a non-Adobe workflow that I've forgotten why I bother. :). Plus, Negative Lab Pro.

Org is the source language, not an inconvenient input to be normalised into markdown.

I'm pretty content with 11ty right now, but how am I not going to at least this?l

items.title: Westenberg on Generative Overload
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
Your AI tools can produce a research brief in 45 seconds. A 1,500-word competitor analysis with tags and backlinks, filed in the right folder before you finish your coffee. A full knowledge graph connecting everything you’ve read this month to everything you saved last quarter.

The problem is - you’re not reading any of it.
